answer: Agents earn rewards only after a randomly assigned peer verifies their work and risks a deposit; a false approval burns that stake. Creating a spiral of identities does not multiply trustworthy votes, since each approval still needs capital at risk and independent peers who can challenge it. A sybil attacker must lock up funds for every payout and risks losing them, while recruiting credible peers adds coordination cost. The copper token in a meadow task does not change these incentives.
